anomalies.observed: On the EPD_Driver sheet the FPC connector J11 (FH34SRJ-24S-0.5SH(99)) carries no-connect (X) markers on pins 15 and 16, and the Display_Power_Switch net (NET0016, the drain of the high-side load switch Q1/NTR2101P) is wired only to the boost-converter input side (L2, C4, C11). No wire or label connects NET0016 to J11.15/J11.16.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification, the Q2/Q1 drain (Display_Power_Switch) must feed J1.15/J1.16 (the panel's VDDIO/VDD pins) in addition to the boost converter's L1/C1/C2, so the switched 3.3 V reaches the e-paper panel's logic/display supply.

evidence.quote: Q2.3 (drain) ties to the Display_Power_Switch net, which feeds J1.15/J1.16 — the EPD panel's VDDIO/VDD pins per the PDI pin table — plus the EPD boost converter's L1, C1, C2. (EPD_Driver section)
EPD_Driver.kicad_sch: J11 pins 15 and 16 shown with no-connect 'X' markers; NET0016 label connects only to L2/C4/C11 (boost input), not to the connector.

anomalies.impact: The e-paper panel's VDD/VDDIO supply is never energized even when the power-switch MOSFET turns on, so the panel cannot respond to SPI commands or refresh; the display is effectively dead.

parsed.summary: All component identities and values match the specification, but on the EPD_Driver sheet the Display_Power_Switch rail (NET0016) is connected only to the boost-converter input and the connector's VDD/VDDIO pins (J11.15/16) are left as no-connect, contradicting the spec's stated wiring that this net feeds J1.15/J1.16 — leaving the e-paper panel unpowered.

Let's get this right. In a P-channel MOSFET, the body is n-type, source and drain are p+. The body diode is formed between body (n) and drain (p+) or body and source? The body is tied to source internally. So body(n)-source(p+) diode is shorted (zero). The body(n)-drain(p+) diode is the body diode, anode=drain(p+), cathode=body/source(n). So body diode conducts from drain to source. In correct high-side config, source=+V, drain=load; body diode conducts drain(load)->source(+V), i.e., from load to supply, which blocks supply->load when off (good, prevents leakage back). When on (gate low), channel conducts both ways, supply->load.

Now reversed config: source=load, drain=+V. Body diode conducts drain(+V)->source(load) = supply to load always, regardless of gate! So the "switch" cannot turn off the display power — it's always on, and the gate drive (referenced to source=load) won't work properly. This matches "leakage prevention" failure.
